newsitem.title: FRANCE: No link between Lagardere probe, Thomson - Toubon.
newsitem.headline: No link between Lagardere probe, Thomson - Toubon.

text.p: French Justice Minister Jacques Toubon said on Sunday there was no connection between the placing under investigation of the chairman of the Lagardere group and the group's intended takeover of the defence and electronics group Thomson SA.

Jean-Luc Lagadere disclosed in an interview with the daily Le Figaro on Saturday that he had been placed under legal investigation on October 28 in connection with complaints filed by shareholders when his Matra missile unit merged with publishing unit Hachette in 1992.

Lagardere said the complaints against him focused mainly on control exercised over Matra-Hachette by the Lagardere group, a partnership with limited shares, and on a system of fees paid to its managers, he said.
"His being placed under investigation is in absolutely no way connected to the privatisation of Thomson," Toubon told RTL radio.

"Since he is presumed to be innocent, why should any conclusions be drawn linking this with...Thomson and the creation of a giant defence industry group which will be the second largest in the world," Toubon said.
France announced in mid-October that it favoured a takeover proposal from Lagardere for Thomson SA.
It plans to recapitalise Thomson with 11 billion francs before selling it to Lagardere for a symbolic franc.
